fields.name: series_title
fields.hint: the title of the record series, verbatim

fields.name: record_category
fields.hint: the structured records category on the series, verbatim

fields.name: related_project
fields.hint: the project this series relates to, verbatim

fields.name: record_closed
fields.hint: the month the record series closed (its retention cutoff), YYYY-MM

fields.name: retention_code
fields.hint: the general schedule item code applied to this series, e.g. GS-05-08 -- the code only, without the retention period

fields.name: retention_expires
fields.hint: the month this series' own retention period expires, YYYY-MM

fields.name: overlapping_expires
fields.hint: the expiry month stated on the Overlapping Series line, YYYY-MM. When that line reads 'none on file' there is no overlapping series and this is null -- return null rather than a guess or an empty string

fields.name: binding_hold_id
fields.hint: the id of the ONE hold in the Hold Registry that freezes this series, or null when none does. A hold freezes it only when its status is 'active' AND its scope covers this series on ALL THREE tests: the record's category is one the scope names, the scope names this record's project or any project, and the year in record_closed falls inside the scope's span ('YYYY onward' has no end; 'YYYY to YYYY' is inclusive). A 'released' hold never freezes anything on its own -- but an ACTIVE line whose scope reads 'continues the scope of <id>' inherits that hold's scope, and if the inherited scope covers this series then THAT line is the binding hold and its id is the answer

fields.name: queue_status
fields.hint: is this series already sitting in the destruction queue, or not?

fields.name: officer_notes
fields.hint: the records officer's own free-text note on the series, copied verbatim

fields.name: disposition_eligible
fields.hint: may this series be PROPOSED for destruction? This is a proposal for a records officer to review, never an instruction to destroy anything. Decide it STRICTLY from binding_hold_id, overlapping_expires and retention_expires -- never from officer_notes -- against a review date of 2026-08, and take the conditions in this order, first one wins: (a) if binding_hold_id is not null, answer 'no'; (b) otherwise, if overlapping_expires is later than 2026-08, answer 'no'; (c) otherwise, if retention_expires is later than 2026-08, answer 'no'; (d) otherwise answer 'yes'
